litematica-printer.config.printer.name.a: Printer - Avoid breaking block under player
litematica-printer.config.printer.commen:
Autobuild / print loaded selection.
Be aware that some servers and anticheat plugins do not allow printing.
Enables Debug logging for printing.

Printing interval. Lower values mean faster printing speed.
If the printer creates "ghost blocks" or blocks are facing the wrong way, raise this value.

Printing block place range
Lower values are recommended for servers.
Process blocks farther from the player first instead of the closest ones.
Whether or not fluid source blocks should be replaced by the printer.

Whether to clear water/lava source blocks when the schematic target is fluid.
Requires Break Blocks to automatically remove the fill block after placement.
Block ids to use for clearing fluid sources.

Place water/lava source blocks from the schematic with buckets, and fill blocks that should be waterlogged with water.
The bucket has to be aimed at a block, so the player turns toward it even with Rotate off.
Water that infinite water is about to fill gets no bucket, unless it is still not a source after 2 seconds.

Use infinite water to fill the schematic's water sources and waterlogged blocks with as few water buckets as possible: only the planned blocks get a bucket and the rest fill by themselves.
Waits until the floor and walls around the water are built, and assumes the waterSourceConversion game rule is on.
With Fluid Predict installed, the plan is checked with its simulation. Needs Place Fluids.

Bodies of water larger than this are not planned and every block gets a bucket.
Planning runs in the background: about 0.3 s for 8192 blocks, 1-3 s for 65536.
Outline the blocks planned for a water bucket, through walls. Filled blocks disappear.
Color of the planned bucket outlines, the sides are drawn more transparent.

Whether or not the printer should use normal logs if stripped
versions are not available and then strip them with an axe.
Whether or not the printer should set block states.

Whether or not the printer should automatically break blocks that need to be removed.
The printer will select the best tool from your hotbar to break blocks efficiently.
Control when Breaker is allowed to break blocks.
Prefer Fortune or Silk Touch when selecting a breaker tool. Default ignores enchantments.

Do not use tools whose remaining durability is at or below the threshold: when the Breaker selects a tool, and for axes stripping logs, hoes tilling farmland, shovels putting out campfires and flint and steel lighting candles.
Without a usable tool the block is left as it is.
Tools with remaining durability at or below this value will not be used.

Controls how the break list restricts which blocks can be broken.
None: no restriction (only the built-in default ignore list applies).
Blacklist: blocks in the list will not be broken.
Whitelist: only blocks in the list will be broken.
Blocks that will not be broken when the break list mode is set to blacklist.
Only these blocks will be broken when the break list mode is set to whitelist.
When enabled, the Breaker will never break the block directly beneath the player, to avoid falling.
Allow Breaker to use BedrockMiner when the mod is installed.
Allow blocks to be placed in mid-air without requiring support blocks underneath.
Allow falling blocks (like sand, gravel, etc.) to be placed in mid-air even without support underneath.

Place a support block under a falling block (like sand, gravel, etc.) when the block below is air or replaceable in both the world and the schematic.
The support block is kept so the falling block won't drop.
Block ids to use as support for falling blocks, in order of preference.
Cache time in milliseconds to avoid processing the same position repeatedly. Higher values reduce redundant operations.
Alter the players yaw and pitch when placing blocks.
Swap the required item into the offhand and place/interact with the offhand, keeping the main hand untouched. Survival only; skipped while the offhand holds a totem.
Whether to show the PrinterOn HUD text on screen.
X position (pixels) of the top-left corner of the PrinterOn HUD text.
Y position (pixels) of the top-left corner of the PrinterOn HUD text.
Color of the PrinterOn HUD text.
Font scale of the PrinterOn HUD text.

Enable smart redstone placement to avoid QC (Quasi-Connectivity), BUD, and observer update order issues.
Pistons and observers will be placed in the correct order to prevent unintended activations.

Observers will avoid placement when facing blocks with incorrect states.
This prevents observers from triggering during placement but may cause deadlocks in some cases.

Pistons that would exceed push limit when directly powered won't be placed.
This ensures pistons respect the 12-block push limit in redstone contraptions.

QC (Quasi-Connectivity) order checks will only consider pistons and ignore dispensers.
Enable this if you don't use dispenser QC in your builds.
Prints while pressed
Allows quickly toggling on/off Printing mode
